IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager: spike in DNS SERVFAIL/NX for eu-west resolvers via Cloudflare starting ~1715429900. Observed increase in 5xx/error rates for hosted-api-eu routes. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/geo-dns/geo-dns-health
Ava (oncall): I'm on it. Paging SRE + NetEng. Initial impact: elevated latency and checkout errors for a subset of EU customers.
Sam (SRE): seeing ~18% 502s at the API edge for eu-west1. Error distribution skews to clients hitting CF resolver IP ranges 172.65.* and 104.16.*.
Ryder (NetEng): Cloudflare status shows degraded resolver performance in some EU PoPs. Our passive probes show intermittent SERVFAILs for our authoritative NS answers (not consistent across all CF PoPs).
Maya (Support): two enterprise customers reported failed checkouts and increased retries. CS is on standby for customer comms.
Ava (oncall): severity P1 due to revenue/customer impact. Running quick impact query. Kai, can you pull the last 30m of resolver response codes and which PoPs are failing?
Kai (prod-eng): pulling now. snippet from our resolver-probe logs:
```
2026-03-15T12:29:02Z probe-eu-1 CF_RESOLVER=104.16.0.2 ANSWER=SERVFAIL 
2026-03-15T12:29:03Z probe-eu-3 CF_RESOLVER=172.65.1.5 ANSWER=NOERROR (stale)
2026-03-15T12:30:10Z probe-eu-2 CF_RESOLVER=104.16.0.2 ANSWER=SERVFAIL
```
Sam (SRE): confirmed — it's split: some CF resolvers return SERVFAIL, others return cached NOERROR; clients that hit the bad resolvers fall back to other resolvers and sometimes end up routed to non-eu origins -> high tail latency.
Ryder (NetEng): short term mitigation options: 1) Flip GeoDNS priority for eu to prefer Route53 answers (we have a passive DNS layer that can prefer R53 when CF resolvers show degradation). 2) Lower TTL for failover? CF-side TTL is unaffected; our edge caching respects TTL. 3) Broader: ask CF to fail over their resolvers (we've opened a ticket).
Ava (oncall): do #1 now. OpsRunbookBot, show runbook step to force route53 preference.
OpsRunbookBot: Runbook: GeoDNS emergency failover:
1) `rb geodns show eu` -> inspect current weights
2) `rb geodns set-weight eu cloudflare 0`
3) `rb geodns set-weight eu route53 100`
4) Verify with `dig @8.8.8.8 www.redwoodapi.com A +short` and internal probes
Note: changes may take up to our internal cache TTL (~90s) to propagate.
Ava (oncall): executing step 2/3 now.
Sam (SRE): while that's rolling, run manual checks against common resolvers:
```
dig @104.16.0.2 www.redwoodapi.com A +short ; # CF suspected bad
dig @172.65.1.5 www.redwoodapi.com A +short ; # CF other PoP
dig @8.8.8.8 www.redwoodapi.com A +short ; # public fallback
```
Maya (Support): crafting a short customer note: "We're seeing DNS resolver degradation affecting EU traffic; engineers are failing over to an alternate DNS provider and monitoring. We'll provide updates every 15 mins."
Ryder (NetEng): CF ticket opened with reproduction + header traces -> Ticket #CF-8473. Asked for per-PoP resolver remediation.
Kai (prod-eng): after `rb geodns set-weight` propagation we see a drop in eu 5xxs to ~3% within 2 minutes. edge latency trending down.
Ava (oncall): good. Continue monitoring. Sam, keep watch on error budget and rollback if anything unexpected.
Sam (SRE): monitoring logs; watching for any cache-thrashing. Also validating no internal config drift in our authoritative records.
Ryder (NetEng): note: Route53 answers have a longer TTL; this may delay reversion when CF is healthy. Plan to revert once CF confirms stable.
Maya (Support): queued a customer status update to affected accounts and posted a public status update draft to #status.
Kai (prod-eng): small gotcha — one EU POP still reports NX intermittently to probes even after failover; looks like a small subset of resolvers still returning old CF answers due to client-side resolver caches. That's expected until caches evict.
Ava (oncall): next steps: 1) Keep GeoDNS preferring R53 until CF confirms stable and our probes show <1% SERVFAIL across EU PoPs. 2) Exec summary for postmortem. 3) Handoff to night oncall in 1 hour if stable.
Ryder (NetEng): will follow up with Cloudflare on mitigation timeline. Keep me looped for any customer escalations.
Sam (SRE): I'll add temporary alerts to trigger if eu 5xx > 5% for more than 5m.
Ava (oncall): excellent. Thanks all. Filling incident bridge notes now.
OpsRunbookBot: bridge created: https://zoom.redwood.internal/bridge/INC-1715429999
Maya (Support): adding affected customers list to the bridge doc.
Ryder (NetEng): CF updated ticket: partial remediation started for EU PoPs at 12:46Z. They've requested we keep R53 pref prioritized for 15-30 minutes to stabilize.
Kai (prod-eng): last check: eu 5xx now down to 1.2% and key customer checkouts succeeding.
Ava (oncall): moving to monitoring-only. If anything regresses, re-alert. Planning postmortem tomorrow; owners: NetEng + SRE. Handoff to @Liam (night-oncall) in 45m. :thumbsup:
Liam (night-oncall): acknowledged. Will watch overnight and carry PM for postmortem.
IncidentBot: Incident status -> mitigated (failover to Route53). Update: keep as P1 until postmortem and customer followups complete."
